What to test before launching an AI receptionist

Prepare questions, booking rules, escalation paths, lead fields, and review scenarios before an AI receptionist handles customer conversations.

By TurboApply3 min read
On this page
Set a narrow public scope Test complete conversations, not single answers Make the human fallback explicit Launch with review and change control

An AI receptionist should make routine conversations easier without pretending every request is routine. Launch readiness depends on scope, escalation, data handling, and realistic testing more than a polished demo.

Set a narrow public scope

List the questions the receptionist may answer, the actions it may take, and the topics it must hand to a person.

Use approved business information only. The system should not invent availability, prices, policies, medical guidance, or guarantees.

  • Approved services, hours, locations, and contact details
  • Allowed booking and lead-capture actions
  • Topics that require immediate human escalation

Test complete conversations, not single answers

A good first answer can still lead to a poor handoff. Test multi-turn conversations where the customer changes details, asks an unclear question, or decides not to book.

Check that the system summarizes the request accurately and confirms important information before it creates a record or booking.

  • Ordinary questions, corrections, interruptions, and ambiguous requests
  • Contact capture with clear confirmation and privacy-aware handling
  • Booking changes, unavailable times, and cancellation questions

Make the human fallback explicit

Customers should know when a person will take over and what information has already been captured.

The internal team also needs a clear queue, owner, and priority rule. Escalation that only sends an unstructured transcript creates more work instead of reducing it.

  • Visible handoff language for the customer
  • A structured summary for the assigned person
  • A safe path when booking, CRM, or notification tools are unavailable

Launch with review and change control

Start with a bounded audience or schedule, review real conversations, and change one part of the flow at a time.

Record the prompt, knowledge source, routing rules, and test cases so a future update can be compared with the approved baseline.

  • An approved test set for ordinary and high-risk requests
  • Conversation review with private-data boundaries
  • Versioned operating notes, owners, and rollback steps

Keep the next step practical

The goal is not to make every conversation fully automatic. The goal is to answer routine questions reliably, capture useful context, and bring a person in at the right moment.
